title: Quantum Algorithms for Multivariable Polynomial Transformations: From Efficient Synthesis to Quantum Channel Transformations
authors: Zheyu Shen, Yusen Wu, Xiao Yuan, Xiao-Ming Zhang, Yukun Zhang
abstract: Polynomial transformations are basic primitives in quantum algorithms: quantum signal processing and singular value transformation compile univariate polynomials into circuits with query complexity essentially set by degree. Multivariable transformations of noncommuting matrices, however, lack a comparable synthesis theory. We develop a complete constructive theory under joint block access for all polynomials contractive on the prescribed matrix domain. Given a compact finite-state description of a degree-$D$ polynomial $P$ and $0<τ<1$, we synthesize $P$ with $(1+τ)$-optimal normalization using $O(D/\sqrtτ)$ queries, and exactly $D$ under row-block access, matching a degree lower bound. The complete circuit realization is classically computable in polynomial time with polylogarithmic dependence on accuracy. The key to our construction is a finite algorithmic Schur--Agler theorem: the coefficient recurrence defines a polynomial-dimensional continuation space supporting a complete semidefinite certificate for contractivity on the prescribed domain. Factoring this certificate yields the contractive realization underlying the query algorithm.   Beyond matrix transformations, our framework lifts multivariable polynomial synthesis to quantum channel transformations. Given coherent Kraus access $K=\{K_a\}_a$, we synthesize any finite jointly contractive family of noncommutative polynomial maps $K\mapsto\{F_b(K)\}_b$ as completely positive operations, allowing coherent interference among Kraus histories. Furthermore, channel-level transformations specified by causal Choi data can be synthesized explicitly as fixed-order quantum combs. Collectively, these results point to a broader program: multivariable approximation as a language for multi-operator quantum algorithms and higher-order quantum information processing.
summary: This paper establishes a comprehensive theory for synthesizing quantum circuits implementing multivariable polynomial transformations on noncommuting matrices. It achieves optimal query complexity bounds and extends the methodology to synthesize complex quantum channel transformations. This work positions multivariable approximation as a fundamental language for designing higher-order quantum information processing protocols.
main_problem: Developing a complete constructive theory for synthesizing multivariable polynomial transformations of noncommuting matrices, and extending this framework to quantum channel transformations.
main_result: The authors provide a synthesis procedure achieving optimal query complexity for these transformations and show how this framework can synthesize any jointly contractive family of noncommutative polynomial maps as completely positive quantum operations.
method: The core method involves developing a finite algorithmic Schur–Agler theorem to derive a semidefinite certificate for contractivity, which then dictates the structure of the required quantum query circuit.
model_or_system: The work focuses on quantum algorithms utilizing polynomial transformations applied to noncommuting matrices and generalized to quantum channels described by Kraus operators and Choi data.
key_observables: Query complexity ($O(D/\sqrt{	au})$ or $D$), contractivity certificate, and the resulting quantum channel operations.
important_parameters: Degree $D$, contraction parameter $	au$, and the number of joint accesses.
main_assumptions: The synthesis relies on a compact finite-state description of the polynomial and the existence of a joint block access model.
figures_summary: The notes mention figures illustrating the interleaved structure of the complete quantum circuit and the definition of the Gram matrices used in the fixed-query criterion.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the lack of a synthesis theory for multivariable transformations to developing the constructive theory using the Schur–Agler theorem, and finally applying this theory to synthesize quantum channel transformations.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous mathematical framework for designing complex quantum circuits by treating multi-variable polynomial operations as a structured, synthesizable resource, which is crucial for advanced quantum algorithm design.
